Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Two follow-ups from our engineering team as we map the POC to our clinical transcription pipeline:  

1) Time-to-first-token (we measure from TCP accept to first generated token) — we need consistent first-token latency under 150ms for 95% p95 during business hours for 99% of short requests (<=128 tokens).
2) Sustained token throughput — the transcription service expects bursts to 100+ tokens/sec for short windows and sustained 50 tokens/sec per connection for longer sessions.

Can Redwood commit to different SLAs for streaming endpoints vs the non-streaming (sync) API? If not, what carveouts or exception process do you recommend — we need this documented for our procurement team.

Also looping procurement for contract language and any performance appendices.

Team —

I ran a quick feasibility check with infra: baseline hosted API (multi-tenant) cannot promise 150ms p95 first-token for streaming at scale because of tenant co-location and dynamic batching. Typical hosted p95 first-token for small-batch streaming under our best-case model+region is ~180-300ms depending on model. Sustained token/sec guarantees are similarly constrained (we don't make per-connection token/sec guarantees in hosted).

Options to offer Acme:
1) Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs with guaranteed slice): realistic to commit to p95 first-token <=150ms for short sequences when pinned to a dedicated instance, plus a sustained per-connection target of 50 tokens/sec — subject to a documented burst window (e.g., 60s burst at 100 tokens/sec) and a capacity plan.
2) Hosted with priority routing + burst credits: not a strict SLA; we can provide an operational objective and credits if we miss it, but this is not recommended for procurement language that requires hard guarantees.
3) Hybrid: streaming endpoint on Dedicated during business hours, fall back to non-streaming batch transcription outside SLA window; include explicit fallback behavior in appendix.

I attached a short appendix (SLA_Streaming_NonStreaming_Tradeoffs.pdf) with measurement definitions and a sample clause for procurement. Let's choose a path and I can draft the concrete contract wording.

Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Tom —

Adding a bit more technical clarity from Solutions/Platform so your SREs and procurement have measurable language. Please see the definitions and the proposed acceptance criteria below. Happy to iterate.

Measurement definitions (how Redwood will measure):
- "First-token latency": measured at Redwood edge as time from our request-accept timestamp to the first token byte emitted on the streaming socket; reported at p50/p95/p99 for given time windows.
- "Sustained token rate": measured per connection as a rolling 60s average tokens/sec. Sustained guarantees apply when average sequence length > 256 tokens; bursts are defined as instantaneous 5s windows where token/sec exceeds sustained target.

Proposed acceptance criteria (Dedicated pool scenario):
- First-token latency: p95 <= 150ms for requests <=128 tokens during business hours (08:00–20:00 PT), measured over a rolling 30-day window.
- Sustained rate per-connection: guaranteed 50 tokens/sec sustained; allows 60s burst at up to 110 tokens/sec.
- Outage/fallbacks: if dedicated pool falls below health threshold (node OOM, unplanned maintenance), Redwood will route new sessions to a warm fallback (non-streaming endpoints) with best-effort completion and crediting per the appendix.

Operational controls we will include in the appendix:
- Prometheus metrics and token-level traces for your SREs to ingest (read-only streaming view).
- Canary rollout windows for model upgrades and a 24-hour no-rollout restriction during first 30 days of production.
- Mutually agreed ramp schedule for initial commit and scale up.

If Acme wants stricter numbers (e.g., 120 tokens/sec sustained), we will need to size Dedicated GPU class and update pricing. I can work with Infra to produce a capacity/price estimate once you confirm target sustained rate.

—Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
